featured_reviews.review_text:
Located in Andheri West, Mumbai, Kamlakar Panth Walawalkar Udyan is a beautiful 5.6-acre green space with a unique concentric layout and a coveted sand track—perfect for walkers and joggers!

There’s a small area for yoga workouts and stretching, making it a great spot to relax and exercise.
A small pond with ducks adds to the garden’s charm.

There are separate male and female washrooms, plus a water cooler for your convenience. Rules and regulations are well-enforced, ensuring a safe and clean environment.

Nearby: Oshiwara Metro Station (15-min walk), Ram Mandir Railway Station (1.6 km)

Bus Stops: 205, 290LTD, 464LTD nearby

featured_reviews.name: Smitha Renny
featured_reviews.review_text:
I walked about 15 min from my place to reach this beautiful and serene haven. Rich in foliage, this park is a favourite among not just the neighbours, but people living far too.

There's a dedicated jogging path which offers you a soft landing.. ideal for jogging... There are several exercise machine too which help you exercise without going to expensive gyms... Also offering the serene and lush green environment which is so recommended for exercise and workout.

Once you've sweated it out, you can relax and cool down on the several swings that are installed all around the park. Yoga enthusiasts have a dedicated area which is cemented and has a concrete canopy offering you a really cool and breezy surrounding to get relaxed with yogic exercises and postures. The huge Banyan trees in the central area of the park provide a thicket of cool space where you can relax, read your favourite book, listen to music or discourses or even hear a narrated story on your smart device.

The small and artificial lake provides soothing comfort(though the water is in need of treatment and regular circulation). The bridge over the lake too is a picturesque sight.

In all, its truly a place to exercise your body and compose your mind.
I came back energized and yet calm.. Do take out time and visit... You won't regret it.

featured_reviews.name: Derishta Pillay
featured_reviews.review_text:
At the outset I must say that neither myself nor my husband are huge fans of the usual guided walking tours mainly because we hate being taken to cliched and crowded tourist hotspots, listening to facts straight from the Wikipedia page and jostling for space with other tourists just to return sunburned and underwhelmed. In addition we'd already spent a hectic 5 weeks in India - we were tired, grumpy, waiting to fly back home and not at all looking forward to our last 4 days in Mumbai at all. So basically when our travel companions insisted we book a tour - the scene was set for disaster...
'Bombay Walks' single handedly turned this around and Mumbai actually turned out to be the highlight of our trip! (Nope this is not a sponsored review 😂)

The tour: Arpan's tour extends to the days before and after the actual tour as he offers valuable advice about where to stay/eat/party/shop etc. He speaks perfect English, is pleasant and very easy to communicate with. His passion and love for the city is infectious and you will end his tour enthralled, overwhelmed and completely charmed by Mumbai and it's people - vowing to come back and dig deeper, spend longer and see more. The city tour covers many facets of the city - traveling to hidden gems and local landmarks across the length and breadth of Mumbai. You get to see and experience aspects of Mumbai that you'd never be able to do alone with a guide book or google maps - like traveling on local trains and walking through Worli fishing village and stopping by at small off-the-beaten path temples and churches.

The guide: Arpan is reliable, trustworthy and comes well prepared for the type of group. His talking style is light-hearted and easy going but still knowledgeable and always engaging. He's the type of guide that can tell you interesting facts about the history, architecture and politics of a place but also where to get the best coconut water along the way and which public toilets are ok to use.
We only met Arpan in person on the day of the tour and although we were constantly bombarded with sights, sounds and smells (it is Mumbai after all) - it never once felt like we were just being dragged from point to point whilst he rattled off information but rather that we were spending the day walking around with an old friend.

Target travelers: We're fairly well travelled and yet this is the first time we've ever bothered to leave a tour review - on any platform - I think that in itself indicates how highly we recommend this tour.
This is really a 'must do' in Mumbai.
It's so good we would do this tour again even if it were to cover the exact route we already took. The walking wasn't particular strenuous so it's recommended for any age group it should also be noted that we found that     Arpan was discreetly always conscious of where the group members were and their safety and constantly aware of our surroundings and the locals around us - on that note I would recommend this tour even if you're a single female traveling alone.

When to do it: Try and do this tour on your first full day in Mumbai because it's also a great way to orientate yourself around the city and plan the rest of your time there.

That city that everyone talks about - that's all of India's many faces and layers in one, that accepts everyone, that's everyone's home - regardless of language, religion or creed - Mumbai is THAT city and you'd be crazy if you miss the opportunity to let a born-and-bred local guide you around...

customer_updates.name: Explorewithrohitmaurya
customer_updates.text:
The Malabar Hill Elevated Nature Trail offers a calm and well-managed experience, especially for those looking for a quiet break from Mumbai’s chaos.
The entry and exit process is smooth, well-organized, and handled professionally. The security staff deserve special mention—they’re polite, helpful, and clearly serious about their responsibility, which adds to a feeling of safety and discipline.
The walkway itself is quite small, and this is where expectations need to be realistic. While many trees and birds are tagged with names, actual wildlife sightings are limited. During my walk, I only spotted Indian parrots and crows—interestingly, two types of crows: one completely black and another with a grey neck, the kind commonly seen across the country.
The environment is quiet and peaceful, and you do feel good walking there. However, it is not very dense or forest-like, which was a disappointment for me. If you’re expecting a rich, immersive nature trail, this may feel underwhelming. The short length of the walkway further adds to that feeling—it ends just when you start settling into the experience.
Overall:
A neatly maintained, calm space with good management and discipline. Best suited for a short, relaxed walk and first-time visitors. Don’t expect dense greenery or a long trail—think of it as a brief nature pause rather than a full escape into the wild.

featured_reviews.name: Pratik B.
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited the Malabar Elevated Nature Trail yesterday and it turned out to be a beautifully planned and refreshing experience. It offers a completely different perspective of Mumbai compared to the usual views from Nariman Point or Marine Lines. This side feels quieter, greener, and far more immersive.

I had booked the 6 am to 7 am slot to catch the sunrise, and it was absolutely worth it. Around 6:13 am, the trail slowly transitioned from darkness to soft morning light and then into a warm sunlit path. Watching that gradual change while surrounded by greenery made the experience feel very special. Even in peak summer, the trail remains surprisingly lush.

At that hour, the environment is calm and soothing. You can hear birds chirping, feel the gentle sea breeze, and enjoy a peaceful start to the day before the city gets busy. The weather is generally pleasant early on, though a bit of humidity is possible depending on the day.

One thoughtful aspect of the trail is the informative signage placed along the way. There are well designed metal information panels that describe the trees, plants, birds, insects, and small wildlife you might come across, with details provided in both Marathi and English. It adds an educational layer to the walk and helps you connect more deeply with the surroundings.

A few things to keep in mind. Entry is strictly through pre booked tickets, so it is best to book a few days in advance as there is no on the spot booking. There is no parking available, so public transport is the way to go. Your ticket is required for both entry and exit, so keep it handy and make sure your phone is charged.

Visitor numbers are limited to around 200 people per slot, which helps maintain the peace and cleanliness of the space. The trail is currently very well maintained, and it would be great if everyone continues to respect that.

It feels like a thoughtful initiative inspired by places like Singapore, and credit to BMC for creating something like this in the city. Hopefully, more such spaces come up across Mumbai.

Overall, this is a must visit if you enjoy nature, calm surroundings, and unique views of the city.

featured_reviews.name: Sarvesh Salunkhe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Veermata Jijabai Bhosale Udyan and Zoo (Rani Chi Baug) recently. The zoo is a good place for a family outing and children can enjoy seeing various animals and birds. The garden area is green and peaceful, making it suitable for a short walk.

However, some sections could be better maintained, and a few animal enclosures appeared smaller than expected. Due to crowds, especially on weekends, the overall experience can feel a bit rushed. Facilities and signboards could also be improved for visitors.

Overall, it’s a decent place to spend a few hours in Mumbai, particularly for families with kids, but there is room for improvement.

featured_reviews.name: ameya mahadik
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a fantastic visit to Veermata Jijabai Bhosale Botanical Udyan and Zoo. The place offers a perfect blend of nature, history, and wildlife. The botanical garden is lush, well-maintained, and home to a wide variety of trees and plants, making it a refreshing escape in the heart of Mumbai.

The zoo is equally impressive, with a good collection of animals including tigers, hippopotamuses, crocodiles, deer, and many other species. The biggest attraction for me was the penguin enclosure. Seeing penguins up close was a unique experience and one of the major highlights of the visit.

The premises are clean, the animal enclosures are well organized, and there is plenty of information available for visitors. It's a great destination for families, children, wildlife enthusiasts, and anyone looking to spend a day surrounded by nature.

Overall, it was an enjoyable and memorable experience, and I would highly recommend visiting if you're in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Rehan Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Had a great experience at Rani Bagh. The zoo is clean, well-maintained, and surrounded by beautiful greenery. There is a good variety of animals and birds, making the visit both enjoyable and interesting. The atmosphere is peaceful, and it is a wonderful place to spend time with family and friends. Overall, a very pleasant and memorable visit. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Rohit Parui
featured_reviews.review_text: I absolutely love Veermata Jijabai Bhosale Botanical Udyan and Zoo. I highly recommend everyone to go and spend some quality time here with friends, family, and kids. It is a wonderful place where you can see a rich variety of different birds, animals, and beautiful trees. Beyond just being a fun day out, it is incredibly educational for kids as they can easily gain a lot of knowledge about nature and wildlife while exploring the beautiful grounds..

featured_reviews.name: Abir Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
The place is well-maintained, but it feels more like a garden than a proper zoo due to the limited number of animals. There is only one tiger and one leopard, and several key animals are missing—there are no elephants, lions, or giraffes. The bird section also has very few species, although penguins are available, which is a plus.

The area is clean and spacious, and the food options inside are good. However, basic facilities like access to cold drinking water should be improved. Considering the large number of visitors and the strong revenue potential, the management should focus on adding more animals and enhancing overall maintenance to make the experience more worthwhile.

featured_reviews.name: Uday Pasupuleti
featured_reviews.review_text: Veermata Jijabai Bhosale Botanical Garden and Zoo is a wonderful attraction in Mumbai, combining beautiful greenery with an exciting wildlife experience. The garden is well maintained with lush landscapes, rare plants, and majestic old trees that make every walk refreshing. The zoo's major attractions include the penguins, Bengal tiger, leopard,Hippo,Bear, crocodiles, monkeys, deer, and a variety of colorful birds. Watching the penguins is especially a delight for both children and adults. The entire facility is clean, organized, and educational, making it an ideal destination for families, nature lovers, and photographers. A must-visit place to enjoy nature and wildlife in the heart of Mumbai

featured_reviews.name: Sana Pathan
featured_reviews.review_text: Lovely for a family visit especially with small kids. Good to see water fountains all around and decently maintained animal shelters... the children park is a good size albeit with quite a few swings broken and not well maintained... look into that please so kids can have thier share if fun

featured_reviews.name: Aditee Kale
featured_reviews.review_text:
VeerMata Jijabai Bhosale Udyan is a perfect place to visit for an enjoyable zoo experience in Mumbai. The zoo is well-maintained and offers a chance to see a wide variety of animals in a pleasant and engaging environment.

It houses animals such as tigers, leopards, sambar deer, barking deer, turtles, tortoises, and many more providing a great learning and viewing experience for visitors of all ages. There is also a dedicated bird park with multiple species of birds, including parrots and other colorful varieties, which is especially delightful. Everywhere there are information boards talking about that specific animal or bird, which becomes helpful for people to know what they are and what are the special / interesting facts about them.

One of the major attractions is the separate, temperature-controlled enclosure for penguins, which is very well designed and adds to the uniqueness of the zoo.

Additionally, the zoo has an in-house canteen that serves good food with a variety of options, including Indian and Chinese cuisine, juices, and chaat, making it convenient for visitors to relax and refuel during their visit.

Overall, it is a great place to spend quality time with family, kids and enjoy a refreshing day close to nature.
